To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cold resistant protein (a member of the CSD family) has a clamp like structure that can bind poly thymidine stretch and can be used in transcription regulation.
cold shock proteins are conserved and the cold resistant protein isolated and characterized from cold tolerant Pseudomonas mutant has an affinity towards poly T stretch.
the CRP from P. fluorescence is a cold shock protein and is involved in transcription regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular modeling of CRP from P. fluorescens, a cold shock protein, to understand the molecular mechanism of its function in the cold resistant mutant.
the structural and molecular characterization of the cold resistant protein isolated and cloned from the cold resistant mutant of a plant growth promoting bacterium, P. fluorescencs.
the structure and function prediction of CRP which can be used as a template for designing new cold resistant proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CRP from the cold resistant mutant of pseudomonas fluorescences is an efficient ligand binding protein and has the ability to bind to RNA and regulate transcription in extreme cold stress conditions.
CRP is a potential candidate for transcription regulation and can be used as a tool for genetic manipulation of cold stress response in plants.
CRP is a novel cold shock protein with a unique clamp like structure that binds to poly T stretch of the mRNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CRP from cold resistant Pseudomonas has an important role in the cold stress adaptation mechanism of this bacterium and the ligand binding site of the protein is located at the cleft formed by the clamp like structure.

the cold resistant mutant of the bacterim P. fluorescencs has evolved to adapt the low temperature by synthesizing CRP, a cold shock protein which has the ability to bind to poly thymidine stretch in the mRNA.
, the cold resistant mutant of the bacterim P. fluorescences has evolved to survive in the cold stress by the presence of a novel cold shock domain protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cold resistant protein from P. fluorescence can be considered a potential target for developing cold tolerant plants.
the structure of CRPs from different cold adapted bacteria are not conserved and hence the mechanism of their functioning may be unique.
, the structure of CRPs can be predicted by insilico approaches and the structure can be used to predict its molecular function.
